attributes.title: Level 1

subgroups.name: solve 1

steps.hints: ❓ Did you check the names of the sprites used in the mySprite.setPosition(x, y) code on lines 20 and 40?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Can a sprite’s position be set before the sprite has been defined?


Solution: 

Sprite names should be swapped in the mySprite.setPosition(x, y) code.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code! 


Notice that the error message on the bottom says the problem is on Line 20: the variable ‘spaceShip’ is used before its definition.



Fix the bugs in the code so that the two sprites appear in different positions when the project is run.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓Did you check to make sure that the name of the sprite in controller.moveSprite(sprite) matches the name of the sprite defined in line 2?
steps.senseiHelp:
❓ What is the name of the sprite defined in the let mySprite = sprites.create(img,kind) code?


Solution: 

The sprite named in the the controller.moveSprite(sprite) code should be changed from “astronau” to “astronaut”.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code! 


Notice that the error message on the bottom says the problem is on Line 21: the program cannot find the name ‘astronau’.



Fix the bugs in the code so that the project is able to start and the astronaut sprite can be moved with direction buttons on the screen.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓Did you turn the effect “on” in the astronaut.setStayInScreen(on) code?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which Boolean turns the stay in screen effect “on”?


Solution: 

false should be changed to true inside the parentheses in the astronaut.setStayInScreen(false) code.
steps.instructions:
When the astronaut sprite moves off the screen, it disappears!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the astronaut stays in the screen as it moves around.

attributes.description: Welcome to Level 1 of Blue Belt! In this level, you’ll move from using blocks to code to using JavaScript, and learn about JavaScript code and syntax! Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 1:

badges.title: And Now For Something New
badges.description: Use the MakeCode JavaScript editor to add sprites and set their properties.

badges.title: Opening Line
badges.description: Write your first line of JavaScript code.

badges.title: Coordinating Coordinates
badges.description: Set a sprite’s position in JavaScript.

badges.title: String Theory
badges.description: Add a string to a function’s parameter in JavaScript.

badges.title: Palette Cleanser
badges.description: Use a number to set the background color of a scene in JavaScript.

badges.title: Truth Hurts
badges.description: Use a Boolean value to set a sprite’s property in JavaScript.

badges.title: Gaining a Following
badges.description: Set a sprite to follow another sprite in JavaScript.
